title: A sharp extension of Halin's removable-edge theorem to matchings
summary: A subgraph $H$ of a $k$-connected graph $G$ is called \emph{$k$-removable} if $G-E(H)$ remains $k$-connected. Halin proved that every $k$-connected graph $G$ with $δ(G)\ge k+1$ has a $k$-removable edge. We extend this result from a single edge to matchings of any prescribed size by showing that, for positive integers $k$ and $m$, every $k$-connected graph $G$ with $δ(G)\ge\max\{k+1,2m-2\}$ contains a $k$-removable matching of size $m$, unless $G\cong K_{2m-1}$, or $(k,m)=(1,2)$ and $G$ is a cycle.
